newsitem.title: USA: Saudi dissident vows "jihad" against U.S. troops.
newsitem.headline: Saudi dissident vows "jihad" against U.S. troops.

text.p: Osama bin Laden, identified by the U.S. State Department as a major world sponsor of Islamic extremism, has vowed to continue waging a "holy war" against U.S. troops in Saudi Arabia.
In a CNN interview broadcast on Sunday, the dissident Saudi Arabian millionaire declared that the United States must pay for its support of Israel.
"We have focused our declaration of jihad (holy war) on the U.S. soldiers inside Arabia," bin Laden told CNN's "Impact" from a location in Afghanistan.
"Even though American civilians are not targeted in our plan. They must leave (Saudi Arabia). We do not guarantee their safety."

Bin Laden, who was stripped of his Saudi nationality in 1994, is wanted by the United States and Saudi Arabian authorities in connection with two bombings in Saudi Arabia that killed 24 U.S. servicemen and two Indian nationals.
He has denied involvement in the two attacks.

Bin Laden first declared "jihad" against the United States in 1996, and Western officials suspect him of links to the mastermind of the 1993 New York World Trade Centre bombing, an attempted bomb attack on U.S. troops in Yemen in 1992 and extremist Islamic activities stretching from Afghanistan to Algeria.
"The U.S. government has committed acts that are extremely unjust, hideous and criminal, through its support of the Israeli occupation of Palestine," bin Laden said.
Saying he felt only "disgust and revulsion" for U.S. President Bill Clinton, he said his comrades inside Saudi Arabia would send the Americans "messages without words."
"I address the mothers of the American troops," bin Laden said. "If they are concerned for their sons, then let them object to the American government's policy."
